claim: Directional microstructures reduce drag primarily through the generation of micro-streams that reduce viscous dissipation.
mechanism: The microstructures create multiple parallel micro-streams that reduce the effective viscosity gradient at the wall. These micro-streams act as low-friction pathways that carry a significant portion of the flow, reducing overall energy dissipation.
evidence: Fish scales create micro-channels that reduce local viscosity
Microfluidic devices show reduced friction with structured surfaces
assumptions: Micro-streams can maintain coherence at Re=500,000
The viscosity reduction effect dominates over other drag mechanisms
expected_failure_modes: Micro-stream disruption at higher flow rates
novelty_rationale: This hypothesis emphasizes micro-stream formation and viscosity reduction rather than boundary layer modification.
testability: Can be tested using particle image velocimetry to visualize and measure micro-stream formation and velocity profiles.
falsifier: If microstructured pipes show no evidence of coherent micro-streams but still maintain reduced drag, this hypothesis is wrong.
